title: P10 writer exclusion was not crash-safe: a process killed inside it left the harness account without DML
what_went_wrong: The first P10 writer exclusion revoked the benchmark account's INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on the fixture and granted them back only in a Python `finally`.
Suite check A20 SIGKILLs a resume in the middle of a restore. The `finally` never ran, so the account kept only SELECT on the fixture.
Every later billing run failed because the form (running as that account) could not save: suite run 1 ended 30/38 with A20-A24, A28, A29 and A12 failing.
root_cause: A safety mechanism that changes persistent server state (grants) was written with in-process cleanup only, while the same suite deliberately kills that process.
detection: P10 suite run 1 (2026-10-18 04:22Z); the wrapper kept the failed fixture (P9 behaviour) and the grant state was read from it before teardown. Evidence kept: evidence/p10/r5_p10_suite_run1_FAILED_20261018T042243Z.md.
impact: Fixture only. Live sik and the ledger were untouched (A13 PASS in run 1); exclusion is refused on live databases in code.

correction.code: The exclusion is recorded in a marker file before the revoke; every oracle start and every restore that finds a marker of a dead process grants the recorded privileges back (WRITER-EXCLUSION recovered). New suite check A31: the account's grants are the same at the end as at the start, no marker left, at least one recovery observed.
correction.verification: Unit test 26/26 (incl. marker recovery); suite run 2 39/39 with A20 recovered and A31 PASS; preservation check PASS.

rule: Any change a tool makes to persistent server state must be undoable by a later process: record it durably before making it, and recover it at the next start.
